short_summary: Former Shin Bet director Ronen Bar has filed a defamation lawsuit against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu over October 7 allegations. Bar contends that warnings were ignored, while Netanyahu points to intelligence misjudgments.

sources.name: Ynetnews
sources.title: Former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar sues Netanyahu over Oct. 7 accusations, reveals ignored warnings

sources.name: JNS
sources.title: 'Shocking lack of understanding': Shin Bet chief unaware of Hamas's intentions, internal report reveals

paragraphs: Former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar has launched a defamation lawsuit against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the Tel Aviv District Court, seeking three million shekels in damages and petitioning the court to dismiss any assertions of prime ministerial immunity. The legal filing, submitted through attorneys Reuven Behar, Yoram Bonen, and Doron Kol of the FBC law firm, accuses Netanyahu of circulating false allegations and promoting conspiracy theories suggesting that the internal security service had possessed advance knowledge of the October 7, 2023 Hamas massacre.

The comprehensive lawsuit addresses the bitter contest over accountability for the catastrophe. Bar openly acknowledges the Shin Bet's failure to furnish the intelligence required to avert the assault, noting that he stepped down with his head bowed before bereaved families. However, he maintains that the prime minister is orchestrating a campaign of baseless manipulation to deflect personal culpability for prolonged policies. According to Bar, Netanyahu disregarded recurrent intelligence warnings throughout 2023 regarding weakening deterrence and the escalating risk of a multi-front conflict. Instead, the prime minister pursued an approach of "quiet at any cost," authorizing continuous Qatari cash transfers that financed Hamas's tunnel construction and weapons procurement despite warnings from the Shin Bet.

The document also details operational grievances preceding the assault. Bar claims his recommendations—such as curbing the entry of Gazan laborers, orchestrating targeted strikes against senior Hamas leadership, and disrupting terror operations in the West Bank—were consistently dismissed or ignored. Bar additionally notes a July 2023 cabinet meeting where certain officials floated permitting Hamas governance in the West Bank, an idea he fiercely resisted. Regarding the night of October 7, Bar stresses that an alert was issued at 3:03 a.m. concerning suspicious border movements, and personnel logged instructions to brief Netanyahu's military secretary, Avi Gil. Bar explains that unlike predecessors Naftali Bennett and Yair Lapid, Netanyahu never furnished his personal mobile number, funneling calls through intermediaries like chief of staff Tzachi Braverman. Netanyahu neither returned communications nor intervened as the disaster unfolded, while barring Bar from consulting then-Defense Minister Yoav Gallant.

Bar further asserts that his relationship with Netanyahu deteriorated after Bar submitted an affidavit to the High Court of Justice warning of potential security risks involving prime ministerial advisers and connections to Qatar, alongside governmental attempts to deploy the Shin Bet against civilian political protests. Having remained silent for three years while waiting in vain for an independent state commission of inquiry, Bar argues that litigation is now the sole avenue to force the disclosure of intelligence records and counter official attempts to alter historical narratives.

The bitter dispute escalated following a September 28 social media post in which Netanyahu openly accused Bar of "failures and crimes." Soon afterward, journalist Ayala Hasson aired an internal Shin Bet memorandum on Channel 11, which Netanyahu publicly circulated. The report, titled "Consultation regarding the management of negotiations for a long-term ceasefire with Hamas," showed that two days prior to the onslaught, Bar was heavily engaged in deliberations regarding a durable truce with Yahya Sinwar.

facts.fact: Former Shin Bet chief Ronen Bar filed a 3 million shekel defamation lawsuit against Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu in the Tel Aviv District Court.
The lawsuit accuses Netanyahu of spreading false claims and conspiracy theories suggesting the Shin Bet had advance knowledge of the October 7, 2023 attack.

Bar acknowledges the Shin Bet failed to provide the intelligence needed to prevent the attack, leading to his resignation, but argues Netanyahu is deflecting responsibility for his containment policies.
Bar claims he repeatedly warned Netanyahu throughout 2023 about weakening deterrence and escalating conflict, but recommendations for offensive actions were dismissed.
On the night of October 7, the Shin Bet issued an alert at 3:03 a.m. and updated military secretary Avi Gil, while Netanyahu had not provided Bar with a direct phone number.
Bar states he turned to the courts because Netanyahu has blocked the formation of an independent state commission of inquiry.

Netanyahu accused Bar of failures and crimes on social media and subsequently shared a Channel 11 report showing an internal Shin Bet document from two days before the attack discussing long-term ceasefire arrangements with Hamas.
